title: Joe Root achieves what no batter has done in 147 years of Test cricket
content: In an impressive display of skill, Joe Root not only surpassed two thousand runs in fourth innings but also became the first cricketer to net one thousand Test runs at Edgbaston. His unbeaten sixty-two propelled England to victory against Pakistan, marking his sixty-ninth Test fifty—an achievement that puts him ahead of Sachin Tendulkar in the record books. Root continues to break records and redefine Test cricket achievement.

title: China has switched on 2,000 servers under the sea that nobody is allowed to touch
content: China has put a 24MW underwater data centre into commercial operation off Shanghai, sinking roughly 2,000 servers into pressure-resistant modules cooled by seawater and powered directly by an offshore wind farm. The Rs 2,000 crore Lingang facility claims a PUE under 1.15 and zero freshwater use. It builds on Microsoft's Project Natick, which sank 855 servers off Orkney in 2018, recorded one-eighth the failure rate of land servers, and was later abandoned.

title: Google just moved 90 people out of DeepMind, and staff are asking why
content: Google is moving its roughly 90-person AI responsibility team out of Google DeepMind and into its global affairs organisation, the division that handles policy and lobbying. The shift, starting in September, is part of a wider reorganisation that folds DeepMind closer into central Google. Some employees worry the team will lose access to Gemini researchers, weakening AI safety work. Team lead Helen King says access and resources stay intact.

title: 'I don't cry for my real life': Smriti Mandhana's straight reply
content: Smriti Mandhana has not spoken publicly about Palash Muchhal, the man she was supposed to marry. During a recent podcast with Shamani, she was asked about the hardest night of her life. Mandhana took a long pause before making it clear that she wanted to speak only about cricket.

title: Texas family donated 100 acres; $145 million sports complex now taking shape
content: A Texas family's generous land gift is becoming a major sports and recreation complex. This $145 million project will serve as a neighborhood hub and tournament destination. Construction is progressing towards a significant milestone with a topping-out ceremony next month. The expansive facility will feature numerous indoor courts and outdoor fields for various sports. This new complex promises to draw visitors and boost local economic growth.

title: Anthropic researcher says humanity's future decided on 'MacBooks of engineers'
content: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has quit the AI industry, saying OpenAI and Anthropic are racing to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. His post, now past 155 million views, has pulled two more AI safety researchers out of Anthropic and Google and drawn a pacing plan from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, backed by Sam Altman and Elon Musk. Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger puts the odds AI kills everyone above 10 per cent.

title: In 2001, Bear Grylls bought a £95,000 Welsh island and rebuilt its only home
content: In 2001, Bear Grylls bought a remote Welsh island for £95,000 when its only house was a “complete wreck”. He and friends spent four years rebuilding it. The island is now an off-grid family retreat, with the house powered by wind and solar energy and rainwater collected from its roof.

title: 'Is it okay?' PM Modi pauses speech as Xi appears uncomfortable - video
content: At the recent BRICS Summit held in New Delhi, Prime Minister Modi and President Xi focused on strengthening their countries' long-term ties, stressing the necessity of safeguarding peace along the border. The discussions prominently featured the trade deficit and the challenge of market access. Both leaders also committed to boosting cultural and business exchanges to achieve shared growth and prosperity.

title: China’s new anti-drone weapon is laser on wheels: Why it matters for modern warfare
content: In a bold move, China's military is engineering a cutting-edge armored vehicle featuring laser armaments to effectively counter drones in any potential incursions into Taiwan. Concurrently, Taiwan is enhancing its drone technology and increasing defense funding at a swift rate. This evolution in military strategy illustrates critical lessons from recent international conflicts, aiming to safeguard against aerial surveillance and assaults.

title: 6 injured after people jump from building in panic as Delhi factory catches fire
content: A fire in northwest Delhi's Swaroop Nagar injured six people who jumped from a building. The blaze erupted in an adjoining godown-cum-factory manufacturing judo dresses and boxing gloves. Panic spread among residents of the adjacent building, prompting the desperate jumps. All injured individuals were hospitalized and are reportedly out of danger. Firefighting operations successfully extinguished the flames after a swift response.

title: After Trump renames Lake Ontario, Republican wants Lake Erie renamed too
content: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing federal agencies to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” on US maps, documents and databases. Canada has rejected the move, while several US governors have also said they will continue calling it Lake Ontario. The decision comes amid rising trade tensions between Washington and Ottawa.

title: Nigar Sultana’s handshake snub to Harmanpreet backfires as BCB weighs captaincy

The board plans to evaluate her leadership after the Asian Games, taking into account the team’s performance. Additionally, there have been complaints regarding her behavior. Bangladesh faced a setback, losing the semi-final against India by 40 runs.

title: Beijing tightens drone crackdown, bans possession, storage across city from Nov 15
content: As of November 15, Beijing will officially prohibit residents and businesses from owning drones. Existing drone owners must either sell their devices or dispose of them before the deadline. Infringers will face potential confiscation of their drones along with hefty fines. This regulation enhances security measures, significantly restricting drone operations within the city, following previous limitations on unauthorized flights and the classification of all airspace as restricted.

title: Gun-toting Brics summit reel puts Delhi constable under departmental inquiry

The constable is also expected to be relieved of his police responsibilities as this matter is investigated further.

title: London homes are cracking, sinking: How extreme heat is damaging properties in UK capital

Expanding clay-rich soil when wet can lead to dangerous foundation shifts during drier spells. The presence of trees and older homes with shallow foundations exacerbates the risk of ground movement.

title: Nighttime light exposure may change heart structure and function, study finds
content: A new investigation has unveiled that nighttime exposure to artificial lighting can transform heart structure over extended periods. Increased light during the night is linked to a heightened likelihood of heart failure and strokes. It causes small but significant alterations in the thickness of heart muscle. Although some changes can be attributed to disturbed sleep, additional factors are at play.

content: the "announcement" came after dipke was allegedly heckled by a group of people during his visit to Balaghat . dipke mocked the government and announced his resignation as the state's chief minister . he also shared a purported resignation letter addressed to the governor .

title: Air India Bhopal-Delhi flight diverted to Jaipur over technical issue, lands safely
content: the aircraft landed safely at Jaipur and is undergoing checks in line with Air India’s safety standards . Efforts are underway to fly the passengers to Delhi at the earliest . air India apologised for the inconvenience caused to passengers due to the unforeseen situation .

title: Why Xi Jinping skipped PM Modi’s gala dinner at Brics Summit in Delhi
content: Xi Jinping skipped a gala dinner hosted by prime minister Narendra Modi . sources say he was absent from the dinner at Bharat Mandapam . he arrived in new Delhi on saturday and attended the BRICS summit .

title: LA renters are packing their bags: Here’s why more people are leaving than moving in
content: data from online real estate marketplace Zillow analysed rental-page views across housing markets in the us to determine where prospective renters searching in each city were coming from . Las Vegas was the most popular out-of-state destination among Los Angeles renters .

title: Brics embraces AI but leaves job displacement largely unaddressed
content: new Delhi Declaration backs AI-driven growth and worker re-skilling . but it leaves unanswered what happens to jobs lost to automation and AI . the declaration calls AI an "immense opportunity to stimulate economic growth and sustainable development for all"

title: ‘Might makes right’ logic should have been discarded long ago: Xi at Brics Summit
content: Xi said international rules must be written by all countries . he called for the principles of sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs and peaceful settlement of disputes to be upheld . the logic of "might makes right" does not hold .

title: Martha Stewart’s 152-acre New York farm now has 100 chickens and 11 pheasants
content: Martha Stewart bought a 152-acre farmhouse in Katonah, new york, in 2000 . it became a working farm, creative laboratory and carefully managed home for an ever-growing collection of animals . over the next 26 years, the property evolved into Bedford Farm, also known as Cantitoe Corners, with horses, gardens, historic and modern buildings .

title: At 100, Barbara Haig still drives her Mustang, putting caution before age
content: a lifetime of seeing the world Travel has been one of the defining threads of Haig's life . she explored the united states and the world with a close friend she met through church . at an age when many people are content to slow down, she is still putting the top down .

title: Noida DM moves SC against HC's 'dystopia' rebuke over student's detention under NSA
